LoginComponent dispatches Login. On success ReceiveAPIAccessToken runs Navigate([redirect || '/']), and '/' is a redirectTo to 'projects', so /projects is reached through a redirect. The app-bar link at app-bar.component.html:9 is hidden on /login.

The app-bar link to /user-settings is hidden on /login because the bar renders only when authenticated. The real path is the stored redirect. A signed-out user who opens /user-settings hits AuthGuard, which dispatches MustLogin(state.url) (auth.guard.ts:18). MustLogin stores redirectTo='/user-settings' and navigates to /login (auth.state.ts:322-323). On /login, the form submit dispatches Login (login.component.ts:42). After HTTP success this runs ReceiveAPIAccessToken, which dispatches Navigate([redirect || '/']) and lands on /user-settings. It works only after that bounce, but the source fully gives the path.

onCreateEvent (form ngSubmit) calls router.navigate(['/my-Events']) once both createEvent and addToMyEvents succeed. That target matches the 'my-Events' child route of the '' layout route. Its 'My Events' dropdown link, routerLink="/my-Events" at header.component.html:29, sits under *ngIf="isLoggedIn". That condition is true on /create-event, because AuthGuardService admits only when currentUser != null, and currentUser can only be non-null after loginStatus$ has emitted true.

The only link to /register in the components shown on /create-event is the header's Sign up link, routerLink="/register" under *ngIf="!isLoggedIn" (header.component.html:20). AuthGuardService on the create-event route admits only when authService.isLoggedIn() (currentUser != null). currentUser is set only together with loginStatus true, either in setUser or in the constructor's sessionStorage path, so the header's isLoggedIn is true and the link stays hidden while the user is on the screen. Logout (header.component.ts) clears the status but immediately navigates to /login, so the link shows only for a transient moment during that navigation, which does not count. Nothing else shown there navigates to /register: CreateEventComponent navigates only to /login and /my-Events, the footer has only href="#" links, the logo points to index.html, and breadcrumbs appear only in HomeComponent.

The shell sidenav header user menu contains the UserInfo item with routerLink ['/profile'].

The literal /rules route is the top-level 'rules' route from FOLDER_RULES_ROUTES (folder-rules.module.ts:35). provideFolderRulesExtension() adds it to the root config with provideRouter. Its ROUTES providers (through ContentServiceExtensionModule and provideApplicationExtensions) are registered before provideShellRoutes(CONTENT_LAYOUT_ROUTES) in app/src/app/app.config.ts, so /rules matches it first. It renders ManageRulesSmartComponent directly in AppComponent's bare <router-outlet />, without ShellLayoutComponent, the sidenav, or the sidenav header that holds the user menu. The only trigger for /profile in the codebase is the routerLink in user-info.component.html:1. That component is reached only through the 'features.header' user menu in SidenavHeaderComponent. The shell-wrapped rules page is nodes/:nodeId/rules (aca-content.routes.ts:404), which is a different URL. One assumption: this relies on the route order that provideShellRoutes (from the @alfresco/adf-core/shell library, which is not installed) normally produces, with the shell route appended after earlier ROUTES providers.

The search route (aca-content.routes.ts:364) is a child of CONTENT_LAYOUT_ROUTES, which provideShellRoutes wraps in ShellLayoutComponent. The shell renders 'app.layout.sidenav', which maps to SidenavComponent. That includes app-sidenav-header, whose aca-toolbar shows the 'features.header' actions. Among them is 'app.header.more' (UserMenuComponent), a mat-menu whose 'app.header.user' item renders UserInfoComponent, which has [routerLink]="['/profile']". The sidenav is not hidden on search: hideSidenavConditions is ['/preview/'] and minimizeSidenavConditions is empty. The /profile route sits under the same shell with ViewProfileRuleGuard, which returns isLoggedIn() || isOauth(), so a signed-in user on /search can reach it.
The search-libraries route is inside the content shell, so the header user menu is shown. UserInfoComponent has routerLink '/profile', and the guard admits logged-in users.

Blog links exist only in the footer, the about-overview page and the blog posts. showFooter is false for the 'home' route, so the footer is not rendered. '/' is redirect-only (to /workloads). The kd-search form (chrome/search/component.ts:45) sits in the chrome shell, which is never shown while the URL is '/'.

After a successful login, login() calls historyService.goToPreviousState('workloads'). That does navigateByUrl(previousStateUrl_), the URL AuthGuard saved when it bounced the user to login. A user who first opened /overview while signed out lands on /overview. The target is not hard-coded, and the code does not restrict it to /overview.

Clicking Sign in on /login calls login() (component.ts:53), which runs historyService.goToPreviousState('workloads') after the HTTP login succeeds. That calls navigateByUrl(previousStateUrl_) (history.ts:52). previousStateUrl_ comes from the pairwise NavigationEnd tracker (history.ts:36). Example: a user on /search?q=x signs out from the chrome user panel (authService.logout navigates to /login), or a 401 makes error/handler.ts:57 navigate to /login. Logging back in then goes to /search?q=x. Correction to the reader's mechanism: AuthGuard.pushState sets previousStateUrl_ equal to currentStateUrl_ (extractedUrl.toString() equals initialUrl.toString() under the default UrlHandlingStrategy), so that path falls back to 'workloads'. The verdict still holds through the history path. The chrome search form itself is not shown on /login.

ChromeComponent is the routed parent of every child route under AuthGuard, /clusterrolebinding included. The other 'overview' paths are historyService.goToPreviousState('overview') at line 217, reached only from the namespace-change dialog, and shouldShowNamespaceChangeDialog also needs resourceNamespaceParam. The remaining ones are in the create components, which are not shown on this screen. No nav, breadcrumb or redirectTo points to /overview.

That lands on the root /login route, and LoginGuard admits the user because they are now unauthenticated. The button is hidden only when the user signed in through an auth header.

Real, but only through the deep-link restore. Submitting the code calls router.navigate(['/vault']) (../../libs/auth/src/angular/new-device-verification/new-device-verification.component.ts:172). /vault sits under the UserLayout route, whose guards are [deepLinkGuard(), authGuard] (oss-routing.module.ts:682). deepLinkGuard saves the URL a signed-out user asked for, and once the user is unlocked it calls router.navigateByUrl with that saved URL (deep-link.guard.ts:39). So a user who opened /settings/security[/session-timeout] while signed out, then logged in and reached this step, lands on session-timeout. /settings/security redirectTo session-timeout (security-routing.module.ts:19). Nothing on the way clears the saved URL: the login-success handler and authGuard's authBlocked path leave it alone. The reader's point that no trigger names settings/security is true, but it does not decide the pair. The hinted sites are wrong: [routerLink]=[] links back to the same page, and the vault rows are not shown here.

Real, but only through the deep-link restore. The UserLayout route's deepLinkGuard (oss-routing.module.ts:682) then calls navigateByUrl with the URL the user asked for while signed out (deep-link.guard.ts:39). Opening /settings/security[/session-timeout] while signed out, then going through login and 2FA, lands on session-timeout; /settings/security redirectTo session-timeout. This is the flow deepLinkGuard was built for. The hinted sites are wrong: a link to the same page, and vault rows that are not shown here.

The anon-layout logo goes to '/', and redirectGuard sends the user on to /vault, /login, /lock or /login-initiated, never to settings/security. The user cannot log in on this page. Real, through the deep-link restore. After a successful recovery-code login the component calls router.navigate(['/settings/security/two-factor']) (src/app/auth/recover-two-factor.component.ts:132). The reader's reason is wrong, but the verdict holds. A sender does exist: DefaultSyncService sends 'convertAccountToKeyConnector' (libs/common/src/platform/sync/default-sync.service.ts:290), and submit on this screen runs loginSuccessHandlerService.run, which does a fullSync. After that, submit navigates to /vault, where authGuard can redirect to /remove-password (auth.guard.ts:108). Both paths require convertAccountRequired$, which needs loggedInUsingSso = tokenService.getIsExternal. /device-verification exists only in a master-password login: it is reached only from LoginComponent (login.component.ts:445), and only PasswordLoginStrategy implements logInNewDeviceVerification. So that condition stays false on this screen and no trigger shown here can reach /remove-password. Caveat: this rests on the client treating the token's 'external' amr as an SSO login; the server that issues the token is not in the repository.

The reader's claim of 'no sender' is false. DefaultSyncService sends 'convertAccountToKeyConnector' after any sync for which convertAccountRequired$ is true (libs/common/src/platform/sync/default-sync.service.ts:290). AppComponent, shown on every screen, handles it with router.navigate(['/remove-password']). On this screen the user can trigger a sync: the Purge vault button opens PurgeVaultComponent, which calls fullSync(true) (src/app/vault/settings/purge-vault.component.ts:65). A server-notification sync can also fire here. In addition, the product switcher's /vault link runs UserLayout's authGuard, which redirects to /remove-password under the same condition (auth.guard.ts:108). The condition depends on backend data that can change during the session: an SSO login plus non-admin membership in a Key Connector org.

The shell sidenav item routerLink ['/remittances/process'] is shown only when *ngIf="mifosRemittanceEnabled", and the target route has remittanceEnabledGuard. The flag is deployment config, and the defaults in the source disagree. assets/env.js sets it false. environment.ts treats unset as enabled, and the Docker envsubst of env.template.js yields '' when MIFOS_REMITTANCE_ENABLED is unset, which counts as enabled. So the deployment decides.
